record.question: They __________ this property for the last twenty years.
record.explanation: Answer B: have owned. “For the last twenty years” describes a state continuing to now; own is stative, so present perfect “have owned” fits. Independent check: A state continuing for twenty years up to the present takes the present perfect “have owned”; “own” is stative and does not normally use the progressive here. Reference: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/grammar/british-grammar/present-perfect-simple-i-have-worked. Verified worked solution, unofficial.
